main_text.l: Corruptio à primariis incipit] Piscis primùm à capite fœtet.
Corruptor] Corruptrix provincia, Cic. Perditor Reipub. Id. Contritor compedum, Plaut. Tritor stimulorum, Id. Confector cardinum, Lucil.
Corruptus] Vitiatus, profligatus, profligatissimus homo. Prolapsus. Constuprata judicia, Cic. Perditissimus homo. Vitiosus, Id. Vitiosissimus, Paterc.
Corruptus muneribus] Argentanginam patitur. Bos in lingua. Percorrumpere donis aliquem, Ovid. Placatus muneribus.
Coruscare, vid. Nitere.
Cortex] Cutis arborum, Plin. Induviæ palmæ arboris, Id. Tunica, Id.
Corvus] Corax, Cic. Ales Satyria, Flor.
Coticula] Lapis Heraclius, Plin. Lapis Lydius. Cotes aurificum, Id. Exhebenus, Id. Index, Ovid. Metallorum examinator.
Cras] Craftinò, Gell. Secundum hunc diem, Cic.
Crastinus] Jam Cras hesternum consumpsimus, etit aliud Cras, Perf.
Crassus] Pinguis toga, Suet. Altus, Cat. Concretus, Cic. Spissus, Virg. Duplex Spina dorsum, i. crassum, Id. Pinguis saliva, Sen.
Crassus (2) vid. Barbarus.
Crasse, vid. Impolite.
Crassescere, vid. Grandescere.
Crater] Patera. Trulla, Cic. Phiala, Juv. vid. Poculum.
Crates] Cancelli, Cic. Cancri, Apul. Clathri cavæ, Hor. Arcus pellucidâ transsennâ, Paul. Interseptum ligneum instar retis, Euseb.
Creare] Natura creat & fingit, Cic. Plasmare, in SS.
Creator] Procreator, molitor, Effector mundi. Sator cœlestium omnium. Conditor ævi Christus, Claud.
Creatura] Res creatæ, Cic.
Creber] Frequens, Quint. Multus, Cic. Crebro crebrius.
Credere] Aliquid credo fore, Plaut. Persuasissimum mihi

page.notes: Faint show-through from the reverse side is not transcribed. The word "Quint." in the entry Creber is partly obscured by a mark in the scan and is uncertain. "etit" in Crastinus appears as printed.
